claim:
Text: "Paul Pogba, who plays for Manchester United and the French national team, retired from international football in response to French President Macron’s comments on Islamist terrorism."
Claim date: October 26, 2020
Claim origin: https://www.195sports.com/%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%84-%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%AC%D8%A8%D8%A7-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D8%AA%D8%B2%D9%84-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%84%D8%B9%D8%A8-%D8%AF%D9%88%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%8B%D8%A7-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D9%85%D8%A7-%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%AB/?utm_campaign=nabdapp.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=nabdapp.com&ocid=Nabd_App
before_justification: The fact-check refutes the claim by confirming that Paul Pogba did not retire from international football; instead, he [publicly denied the reports](https://onefootball.com/en/news/man-uniteds-paul-pogba-slams-fake-news-claims-that-hes-retiring-from-france-duty-31541245), calling them "unacceptable fake news." Evidence shows he [continued to be called up](https://football.fandom.com/wiki/Paul_Pogba) for the French national team after October 2020, and there is no credible evidence linking any decision to retire to President Macron's comments on Islamist terrorism.
after_justification: The claim that Paul Pogba retired from international football due to President Macron's comments is refuted. While some sources initially reported a retirement announcement on [October 26, 2020](https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/paul-pogba-anthony-martial-united-15405360), Pogba and his agent later denied this, and he continued to be selected for and play for the French national team thereafter. Credible news reports confirm that Pogba did not retire in response to Macron's statements, directly contradicting the claim's central premise.

“There’s no place for naivete, nor for fear of Islam which confuses Islamism and Islamic,” he said, calling assuring the security of the French the “raison d’etre” of the country’s diplomatic efforts.
Macron announced the organization of a conference on staunching the sources of funding for terror groups, to be held in Paris in early 2018.
He also argued against taking sides in the regional power battle between Iran, a majority Shiite Muslim country, and Saudi Arabia, a Sunni power.
“Some have chosen [their camp]. It’s a mistake. The strength of our diplomacy is to speak to all sides,” he said.

“There is no alternative to the non-proliferation agenda. It enables a constructive and demanding relationship with Iran,” he said.
